correctness.rationale: For a smooth lattice polygon the source-backed Chern/discriminant expression is \(c(P)=3A-2B+V\). Pick gives \(A=2I+B-2\), while toric adjunction gives sectional genus \(g=I\), so the excess is exactly \(4g+V-4\). The smooth-triangle lemma is proved directly by primitive-edge determinants and forces every smooth triangle to be \(d\Delta\), whose genus is \(\binom{d-1}{2}\). If no such triangle exists then \(V\ge4\), and the rectangle \([0,2]\times[0,g+1]\) realizes equality. The defective \(d=1\) simplex is explicitly excluded, while \(d\ge2\) and all \(g\ge1\) candidates have positive top Chern number and are nondefective.

value.rationale: Projective dual degree and sectional genus are canonical invariants of a polarized surface. The theorem gives a sharp lower envelope over the entire class of smooth toric surfaces at each genus, identifies an arithmetic infinite family of one-unit exceptions, and characterizes the unique equality geometry at those genera as Veronese. This is a natural complete classification rather than a finite census or an arbitrary parameter slice.
